question.problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩,\,t\in [0,\pi ).
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =0 \\ ⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t=0\, & ⇒\,t=\frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)=0\, & ⇒\,t=0,\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is the only solution that satisfies both equations in the domain $[0,\pi )$, so this is the only value of $t$ when the object is stationary.
